blogs.title: Goodbye Tokens, Hello Patches: How BLT Dynamically Allocates Compute
blogs.description: This post breaks down the core innovation of the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT): replacing static tokenization with dynamic 'patching.' We'll explain how BLT uses entropy to group bytes intelligently, allocating more computing power to complex parts of a sentence (like the start of a new thought) and less to predictable parts, resulting in up to 50% better inference efficiency.

blogs.title: Why Your AI Struggles with Typos (And How Byte-Level Models Fix It)
blogs.description: Traditional LLMs often fail when faced with misspellings, weird formatting, or low-resource languages because they rely on a fixed dictionary of tokens. This article explores the 'Robustness' findings from the BLT paper, demonstrating how training directly on raw bytes gives models superhuman abilities in orthography, phonology, and handling noisy input without needing extra training data.

blogs.title: Breaking the Scaling Wall: Growing Smarter Models Without Slowing Down Inference
blogs.description: Usually, making an AI model smarter means making it slower and more expensive to run. This post dives into the 'Fixed Inference Scaling' experiments from the research, showing how BLT unlocks a new dimension for growth: by increasing the size of data 'patches,' engineers can build massive, powerful models that actually run faster than their token-based counterparts like Llama 3.

blogs.title: From Llama to Byte-Latent: Can We Convert Existing AI Models?
blogs.description: Do we need to train everything from scratch? This blog post focuses on the fascinating 'distillation' experiments in the paper where researchers successfully initialized a byte-level model using weights from a pre-trained Llama 3. We'll discuss what this means for the future of AI development and how we might 'byte-ify' existing powerful models to gain robustness instantly.
